subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw support a synchronous plugin-facing pre-persistence config-write veto, and which canonical write paths, ordering guarantees, and failure semantics form that public contract?
rationale: The request adds a new security-sensitive Plugin SDK lifecycle boundary rather than fixing an already-defined broken contract; the supplied maintainer review says the current safeguards do not expose this mandatory external seam.

options.title: Design a narrow shared pre-write hook
options.body: Specify a synchronous rejection-only Plugin SDK hook after core validation and before persistence for all canonical config writers, with stable context and atomic rejection tests.

options.title: Keep validation core-only
options.body: Retain built-in validation and treat wrapper or tool-level validators as advisory rather than introducing a supported mutation interception API.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow shared pre-write hook
recommendation.body: Specify a synchronous rejection-only Plugin SDK hook after core validation and before persistence for all canonical config writers, with stable context and atomic rejection tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied issue discussion records this person keeping the request open and routing the required design decision to the RFC.
